summary: fix(bonusly): reject recipient mentions that won't resolve, via live lookup
reason: Mention syntax is space-free; a syntactic space check alone cannot distinguish a valid single-token mention (e.g. '@jane.doe') from a two-word display name typed as if it were one mention (e.g. '@Jane Doe', this PR's original motivating case) -- both are syntactically 'a token, then a space, then more text'. Iterated through four review rounds on PR #1899: (1) initial whitespace-after-@ check, correct but only caught a literally-empty mention; (2) fixed a stdin bypass of that same narrow check (Greptile P1); (3) a human reviewer correctly flagged that neither version caught the original '@Jane Doe'-shaped case, and a capitalization heuristic considered at that point was rejected as unsafe (it would false-positive on this CLI's own documented example, '+50 @jane.doe Great work...'); replaced the heuristic with a live resolution check against GET /users/autocomplete (F1, this same PR) via a new shared resolveMentionCandidate() helper; (4) Greptile P1 then correctly flagged that the live check was itself silently skipped under --dry-run (the shared client's DryRun flag intercepts every request including reads), so a dry-run preview could still claim success for a mention that would fail live. Fixed by having resolveMentionCandidate flip c.DryRun off for the duration of its own read-only lookup only, then restore it immediately after -- the mutating POST later in the same command is still correctly intercepted if --dry-run was requested, but the validation read now always genuinely hits the live API regardless of --dry-run.
validated_outcome: Live-verified end-to-end, INCLUDING under --dry-run: `recognition create --reason "+15 @Jane Doe test #teamwork"` and the equivalent --stdin payload are rejected before any POST fires, both with and without --dry-run, with live 'did you mean' suggestions pulled from the real directory rather than Bonusly's opaque 'Reason is incomplete' 400. give's --to with a bare unresolvable single token (no embedded space, so the old whitespace check missed it) is rejected the same way, also under --dry-run. A genuinely valid mention (own account's email) passes the check under --dry-run and shows a normal dry-run preview (not a false block), and separately reaches the real API live, which fails for an unrelated, expected reason (self-recognition) -- confirming no false-positive block in either mode.
